raw_case_text:
A 19-year-old Omani female not known to have any significant medical history was referred to our hospital with a history of upper abdominal discomfort more localized to the epigastric region and associated with jaundice and dark urine. There was no history of fever or night sweat nor history of travel. On physical examination, the patient was jaundice; otherwise, the systemic examination was unremarkable.
Complete blood count was within normal limits with a normal white blood count (6.3 10*g/L). Liver function test revealed a picture of obstructive jaundice with a total bilirubin of 52 umil/L, Alkaline phosphatase 302 [iU] /L, and Alanine transaminase 457 [iU]/L. QuantiFERON-Tb gold test was positive.
CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed a lobulated and heterogeneous liver hilar mass with a central necrosis, measuring 2.4 x 3.9 cm. The mass was obstructing the proximal common hepatic duct resulting in dilatation of the intrahepatic biliary tree (Figure 1). The mass was associated with multiple enlarged peripancreatic, porta hepatis and hepatoduodenal lymph nodes, measuring up to 1.2 cm. None of the lymph nodes were showing central necrosis. Features were suggestive of a cholangiocarcinoma of the common hepatic duct. Further work-up with a liver MRI redemonstrated the porta hepatis mass. The mass was T2 hyperintense and T1 hypointense and showed moderate enhancement on postcontrast sequence with severe diffuse restriction (Figures 2 and 3). On MRCP, the mass was causing severe narrowing of the proximal 1.8 cm of the common hepatic duct, reaching the confluence and causing moderate dilation of the intrahepatic biliary tree. In addition, the MRI revealed multiple foci of restriction scattered throughout the liver and some of them showed subtle enhancement on postcontrast sequence suggestive of liver microabscess (Figure 3).Constellation of MRI findings was suggestive of localized TB of the porta hepatis; however, neoplastic lesion such as rhabdomyosarcoma and lymphoma could not be excluded and further evaluation with a tissue biopsy was advised. Chest radiograph was normal. Tumor markers were within normal limits including Cancer Ag 19-9 (CA 19-9): 8U/mL (range, 0-37U/mL), Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA): 1.2 ug/L (range, 0-3ug/L), Alpha fetoprotein: 1.1 ug/L (range 0-15), and Chromogranin A: 47ug/L (range 26-92ug/L)
The patient underwent laparoscopic biopsy and was found to have enlarged porta hepatis lymph nodes. Biopsy was taken from the porta hepatis mass and histopathological examination showed a granulomatous inflammatory process. Although, no definite proof was obtained by culture or polymerase chain reaction (PCR), probable TB diagnosis was made based on the histological and imaging findings, and the patient was treated for 6 months with Rifampicin 150 mg and Isoniazid 75 mg. The patient showed significant response to treatment with dramatic improvement of liver function test. A follow-up liver function test 3 months after starting anti-TB medication showed normalization of Alkaline phosphatase 91 [iU] /L along with improvement of total bilirubin of 24 umil/L and Alanine transaminase 211 [iU]/L. After completion of anti-TB medication, liver function test was back to normal with a total bilirubin of 17 umil/L, Alkaline phosphatase 58 [iU] /L, and Alanine transaminase 16 [iU]/L. A follow-up CT abdomen was performed 10 months later and showed complete resolution of porta hepatis mass and intrahepatic biliary dilatation along with significant regression of previously noted enlarged upper abdomen lymph nodes.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old female presented with upper abdominal discomfort localized to the epigastric region, jaundice, and dark urine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with upper abdominal discomfort predominantly in the epigastric region, accompanied by progressive jaundice and dark urine. She reported no fever, chills, or night sweats.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant past medical history. No travel history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Complained of epigastric discomfort, jaundice, and dark urine. Denied fever, chills, or night sweats. Home medications and allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Jaundiced on general inspection. The systemic examination was otherwise unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: within normal limits with white blood cell count 6.3 x 10^9/L. Liver function tests: total bilirubin 52 umol/L, alkaline phosphatase 302 IU/L, and alanine transaminase 457 IU/L, indicating obstructive jaundice. Chest radiograph: normal. Tumor markers: CA 19-9 8 U/mL (reference 0-37 U/mL), CEA 1.2 ug/L (reference 0-3 ug/L), alpha-fetoprotein 1.1 ug/L (reference 0-15 ug/L), chromogranin A 47 ug/L (reference 26-92 ug/L).
objective.advanced_workup: CT scan of abdomen and pelvis: lobulated, heterogeneous liver hilar mass with central necrosis measuring 2.4 x 3.9 cm obstructing the proximal common hepatic duct and causing intrahepatic biliary tree dilatation, associated with multiple enlarged peripancreatic, porta hepatis, and hepatoduodenal lymph nodes up to 1.2 cm without necrosis (features suggestive of cholangiocarcinoma). Liver MRI and MRCP: porta hepatis mass (T2 hyperintense, T1 hypointense, moderate contrast enhancement with severe diffuse restriction) causing severe narrowing of proximal 1.8 cm of common hepatic duct with moderate intrahepatic biliary dilation, and multiple liver parenchymal restricted foci with subtle enhancement suggestive of microabscesses. Laparoscopic biopsy: histopathological examination of porta hepatis mass showed a granulomatous inflammatory process.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Probable tuberculosis of the porta hepatis presenting as an obstructive hilar mass mimicking cholangiocarcinoma, confirmed by positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold test and histopathology demonstrating granulomatous inflammation; tissue culture and PCR yielded no definite microbiological amplification. Cholangiocarcinoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and lymphoma were ruled out.
Treatment and outcome: Treated for 6 months with rifampicin 150 mg/day and isoniazid 75 mg/day. Liver function tests significantly improved at 3 months (alkaline phosphatase 91 IU/L, total bilirubin 24 umol/L, ALT 211 IU/L) and fully normalized upon treatment completion (total bilirubin 17 umol/L, ALP 58 IU/L, ALT 16 IU/L). Follow-up abdominal CT at 10 months showed complete resolution of the porta hepatis mass and intrahepatic biliary dilatation, with marked regression of upper abdominal lymphadenopathy.
